learning: If line_loss_events stays at 1 with max_error near 0.06 m, the bottleneck is recovery after loss, so the next change will be to line_loss handling or a faster-reacting controller. If line_loss drops to 0 and progress rises, the sensor span was the constraint.
notes: Controller unchanged from baseline to isolate the sensor-span change. Five sensors kept at ±0.03 spacing with 16 mm footprints.
rationale: The baseline (entityR2A, 60 trials) ended every run off_track with exactly one line-loss event, and max_error sat at 0.061 to 0.063 m against the 0.06 m limit. rms_error was 0.023 to 0.026 m, so the robot tracked well until one bend pushed the line out of the array's reach. I accept the Builder's geometry unchanged: sensors at x = ±0.06 and ±0.03 with y = 0.03, 16 mm footprints, and the same wheels, body and mass. The controller is kept identical to the baseline (kp 3.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.2, weights -2 to +2, last_direction) so the race isolates the sensing change. The Builder's own note warns that wider spacing flattens the signal near centre. I am not changing kp yet because the baseline gave no evidence of oscillation (steering_oscillation 0.13 to 0.24), so there is no basis to retune. Expected result, which this race will test: line_loss_events falls toward 0 and more trials stay under the 0.06 m limit. If line_loss stays at 1 with the wider array, the limit is controller recovery, not span, and I will address it next iteration.
